Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) Services at Garden Springs Wellness in Englewood, NJ

Whether you’re impacted by persistent feelings of sadness, intense emotions, or behaviors that seem hard to control, it’s important to know one thing: you don’t have to face this alone. At Garden Springs Wellness in Englewood, NJ, we understand the weight of these challenges and bring a compassionate, evidence-based approach to help individuals break free from cycles of emotional pain and harmful behaviors.

For those dealing with mental health difficulties and dual diagnosis conditions—a combination of mental health issues and substance use disorders—effective, integrative care can make all the difference. Our Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) program is one of the essential tools we use to empower people on their healing journey. Through personalized and structured treatment, DBT provides individuals with skills to stay present, regulate their emotions, and cultivate healthier relationships. At Garden Springs Wellness, we are dedicated to offering support that is both compassionate and effective, helping you envision and create a brighter future.

What Is Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT)?

Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) is a specialized, evidence-based form of psychotherapy designed to treat individuals who experience intense emotional distress, difficulty managing their thoughts and behaviors, or challenges in interpersonal relationships. Originally developed by psychologist Dr. Marsha Linehan to treat borderline personality disorder (BPD), DBT has widely expanded to address a range of mental health conditions, including depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), eating disorders, and substance use disorders commonly seen in dual diagnosis cases.

DBT focuses on teaching practical, actionable skills that reduce emotional suffering and empower individuals to make meaningful changes in their lives. At its core, dialectical behavioral therapy balances two fundamental principles: acceptance and change. Acceptance involves recognizing and embracing emotions or experiences without judgment, while change focuses on actively working to improve thoughts, behaviors, and relationships. This balance of acceptance and change allows individuals to address challenges effectively while fostering self-compassion.

Our DBT therapy program in NJ combines expert therapeutic guidance with personalized care to help individuals rediscover their inner strength and resilience. Our services include individual therapy, group sessions, and tailored treatment plans focused on building skills in four key areas:

Mindfulness helps individuals develop greater self-awareness and emotional grounding, providing a foundation for more intentional decision-making. This practice allows you to slow down, reduce stress, and respond thoughtfully rather than reacting impulsively.

Emotional regulation is defined by Identifying and managing intense emotions in healthier ways. This helps reduce impulsive behavior and promotes stability in daily life. Emotional regulation skills enable you to handle challenging situations without feeling overwhelmed, fostering a greater sense of control and emotional balance.

Distress tolerance teaches you to develop coping strategies to navigate moments of crisis or emotional pain without resorting to harmful behaviors. Individuals will learn to build resilience and respond to stress more effectively. These skills are essential for managing intense emotions in the heat of the moment and for maintaining recovery over the long term.

Improving communication skills, setting boundaries, and building healthier, more fulfilling relationships with others are skills that empower you to express your needs clearly, resolve conflicts effectively, and strengthen the connections that support your mental health journey.
What to Expect at New Jersey DBT Therapy Programs

Starting DBT can be a transformative step toward lasting mental health, but understanding what to expect during this type of therapy can make the process feel less intimidating. At Garden Springs Wellness, DBT typically involves a combination of individual therapy, group sessions, and skills training designed to address both immediate emotional needs and long-term recovery goals.

In these one-on-one meetings, you’ll work closely with a trained DBT therapist to identify and address your unique challenges. Your therapist will help you set goals, monitor your progress, and provide personalized feedback as you develop essential coping skills.

Group sessions provide a supportive environment where you can practice the skills learned in individual therapy. This includes exercises focused on mindfulness, emotional regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Group settings offer the opportunity to learn from others who may be facing similar challenges.

For times when you need immediate support, DBT often includes phone coaching, allowing you to reach out to your therapist between sessions for guidance on applying your skills in real-life situations.

To reinforce the skills learned in therapy, you may be given practical exercises or worksheets to complete outside of sessions. This hands-on approach helps solidify your progress and ensures the skills you learn become second nature.

By integrating these elements, DBT provides a comprehensive approach to mental health that addresses both emotional regulation and behavioral change, helping you build a life that aligns with your goals and values.
The Benefits of Dialectical Behavioral Therapy in Treating Mental Health and Dual Diagnosis Disorders

DBT stands apart as an impactful therapy because of its ability to address immediate emotional needs while fostering long-term stability. Individuals who participate in DBT programs at Garden Springs Wellness experience benefits that bring lasting change to their lives.

For individuals struggling with depression, anxiety, PTSD, or bipolar disorder, emotions often feel uncontrollable or overpowering. DBT provides tools to navigate these challenges with confidence and reduces the intensity of emotional reactions over time. As they learn mindfulness, distress tolerance, and emotional regulation, clients gain the ability to approach their experiences with clarity and calmness.

DBT helps break the cycle of negative thought patterns. For example, someone dealing with depression may feel trapped in self-critical beliefs that keep them stuck. DBT encourages self-compassion and helps reframe those beliefs in ways that pave the way for growth and greater self-acceptance. Similarly, those battling anxiety are supported in facing fears and lowering the grip that worry has over daily life.

Dual diagnosis conditions—the intersection of mental health disorders and substance use challenges—require specialized care to address both underlying causes and immediate behaviors. Without treatment, symptoms of mental illness are often exacerbated by substance abuse, and vice versa. DBT addresses this intersection by combining emotional regulation strategies with behavior-oriented tools for managing cravings, avoiding triggers, and making healthier decisions.

For individuals dealing with substance use disorders, distress tolerance plays a crucial role in maintaining recovery. Stressful moments or crises are common reasons people relapse; however, DBT techniques help individuals tolerate those moments without falling back into old habit cycles. By focusing on mindfulness and acceptance, DBT minimizes self-judgment and creates an environment for sustainable change.

The skills learned through DBT often extend far beyond managing specific symptoms or conditions. Improvements in communication and relationship-building lead to stronger, healthier connections with others. Better decision-making skills empower individuals to take control of their lives, work towards personal goals, and create a sense of accomplishment. Whether the motivator is healing from trauma, overcoming anxiety, improving self-worth, or breaking free from a substance use disorder, DBT provides essential tools for self-discovery and empowerment.
